arxiv-2009-07268.creator: András Gilyén, Zhao Song, Ewin Tang
arxiv-2009-07268.description: Abstract We give a classical algorithm for linear regression analogous to the quantum matrix inversion algorithm [Harrow, Hassidim, and Lloyd, Physical Review Letters’09] for low-rank matrices [Wossnig, Zhao, and Prakash, Physical Review Letters’18], when the input matrix A A is stored in a data structure applicable for QRAM-based state preparation.

arxiv-2111-07316.title: Matrix method of polynomial solutions to constant coefficient PDE’s
arxiv-2111-07316.creator: Victor G. Zakharov
arxiv-2111-07316.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Victor G. Zakharov. In the paper, we introduce a matrix method to constructively determine spaces of polynomial solutions (in general, multiplied by exponentials) to a system of constant coefficient linear PDE’s with polynomial (multiplied by exponentials) right-hand sides. The matrix method reduces the funding of a polynomial subspace of null-space of a differential operator to the funding of the null-space of a block matrix. Using this matrix approach, we investigate some linear algebra properties of the spaces of polynomial solutions.

arxiv-2203-16349.title: The Block-based Mobile PDE Systems Are Not Secure – Experimental Attacks
arxiv-2203-16349.creator: Niusen Chen, Bo Chen, Weisong Shi
arxiv-2203-16349.description: Abstract Nowadays, mobile devices have been used broadly to store and process sensitive data. To ensure confidentiality of the sensitive data, Full Disk Encryption (FDE) is often integrated in mainstream mobile operating systems like Android and iOS. FDE however cannot defend against coercive attacks in which the adversary can force the device owner to disclose the decryption key.

arxiv-2206-14135.description: Abstract . Metaheuristic search algorithms look for solutions that either maximise or minimise a set of objectives, such as cost or performance. However most real-world optimisation problems consist of nonlinear problems with complex constraints and conflicting objectives. The process by which a GA arrives at a solution remains largely unexplained to the end-user.

arxiv-2406-14151.title: Automated detection and mapping of crystal tilt using thermal diffuse scattering in transmission electron microscopy
arxiv-2406-14151.creator: Mauricio Cattaneo, Knut Müller-Caspary, Juri Barthel, Katherine E. MacArthur, Nicolas Gauquelin, Marta Lipinska-Chwalek, Johan Verbeeck, Leslie J. Allen, Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski
arxiv-2406-14151.description: Abstract Quantitative interpretation of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) data of crystalline specimens often requires the accurate knowledge of the local crystal orientation. A method is presented which exploits momentum-resolved scanning TEM (STEM) data to determine the local mistilt from a major zone axis.

arxiv-2411-17802.title: Quantum simulation of the Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev model using time-dependent disorder in optical cavities
arxiv-2411-17802.creator: Rahel Baumgartner, Pietro Pelliconi, Soumik Bandyopadhyay, Francesca Orsi, Nick Sauerwein, Philipp Hauke, Jean-Philippe Brantut, Julian Sonner
arxiv-2411-17802.description: Abstract The Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev (SYK) model is a paradigm for extreme quantum chaos, non-Fermi-liquid behavior, and holographic matter. Yet, the dense random all-to-all interactions that characterize it are an extreme challenge for realistic laboratory realizations. Here, we propose a general scheme for densifying the coupling distribution of random disorder Hamiltonians, using a Trotterized cycling through sparse time-dependent disorder realizations.

arxiv-2503-11606.title: Tensor Products of Quiver Bundles
arxiv-2503-11606.creator: Juan Sebastian Numpaque-Roa
arxiv-2503-11606.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Juan Sebastian Numpaque-Roa. In this work we introduce a notion of tensor product of (twisted) quiver representations with relations in the category of 𝒪 X \mathcal{O}_{X} -modules. As a first application of our notion, we see that tensor products of polystable quiver bundles are polystable and later we use this to both deduce a quiver version of the Segre embedding and to identify distinguished closed subschemes of GL ​ ( n , ℂ ) \text{GL}(n,\mathbb{C}) -character varieties of free abelian groups.

arxiv-2510-16085.title: MoPHES:Leveraging on-device LLMs as Agent for Mobile Psychological Health Evaluation and Support
arxiv-2510-16085.creator: Xun Wei, Pukai Zhou Zeyu Wang
arxiv-2510-16085.description: Abstract The 2022 World Mental Health Report calls for global mental health care reform, amid rising prevalence of issues like anxiety and depression that affect nearly one billion people worldwide. Traditional in-person therapy fails to meet this demand, and the situation is worsened by stigma.

arxiv-2512-01843.title: PhyDetEx: Detecting and Explaining the Physical Plausibility of T2V Models
arxiv-2512-01843.creator: Zeqing Wang Keze Wang Lei Zhang
arxiv-2512-01843.description: Abstract Driven by the growing capacity and training scale, Text-to-Video (T2V) generation models have recently achieved substantial progress in video quality, length, and instruction-following capability. However, whether these models can understand physics and generate physically plausible videos remains a question.

pmc-12521798.title: Chemiexcitation in Ex Vivo Porcine Skin Model
pmc-12521798.creator: Pavel Pospíšil, Vendula Paculová, Ankush Prasad, Michal Berecka
pmc-12521798.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chemiexcitation, the formation of electronically excited states via oxidative chemical reactions, has emerged as a potentially important contributor to skin photobiology beyond direct damage caused by ultraviolet (UV) radiation. This study investigates the hypothesis that UV radiation induces chemiexcitation in skin through the formation of triplet excited carbonyls, which may transfer energy to melanin and contribute to oxidative stress even after the termination of UV exposure.

pmc-13050572.title: MRI Findings of Ovarian Carcinosarcoma: A Retrospective Comparison With Endometrioid Carcinoma
pmc-13050572.creator: Akane Tashiro, Tomohisa Okuma, Taiki Yamaguchi, Takashi Honjo, Nahoko Inoue, Suzuka Okajima, Makoto Murakami, Tomoyuki Ichimura
pmc-13050572.description: PurposeOvarian carcinosarcoma is a rare and highly aggressive ovarian malignancy composed of epithelial and mesenchymal components, and its preoperative diagnosis remains challenging because of nonspecific imaging features. This study aimed to identify MRI findings useful for differentiating ovarian carcinosarcoma from ovarian endometrioid carcinoma by comparing their imaging characteristics.

pmc-13229912.title: Anomalous positional relationship of the superior mesenteric vein relative to the superior mesenteric artery: a cadaveric case report
pmc-13229912.creator: Duc La Minh, Viet Ung Van, Vu Nguyen Hoang, Duy Nguyen Hoang, HuyBang Nguyen
pmc-13229912.description: The superior mesenteric vein (SMV) typically lies to the right of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). We report a cadaveric case in which the SMV was positioned directly posterior to the SMA at the pancreatic head level, then crossed anteriorly to assume a left-sided position at the level of the third duodenal portion (D3).

pmc-13235579.title: Correction: Hygiene procedures of trucks transporting live pigs: multi-assessment validation of a standardized C&D protocol
pmc-13235579.creator: A. Perrucci, A. Magri, V. Cardana, S. Zoppi, C. Cossettini, A. Scollo
pmc-13235579.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). :

“The high prevalence of MRSA even after C&D has been highlighted as a critical One Health issue (60), since MRSA is considered an indicator organism for the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria for both animals and humans (54). In this context, while the transmission of MRSA from truck drivers to pigs has not been conclusively demonstrated (59), available data suggest that drivers are more likely to be victims of occupational exposure than sources of infection.

pmc-13389290.title: Gut bacteria prime and reinforce mature leaf oviposition preference in beetles via plant mediated feedback
pmc-13389290.creator: Chong Li, Ziyue Sun, Yuxin Zhang, Meiqi Ma, Letian Xu
pmc-13389290.description: The gut microbiota can profoundly influence host behavior, yet underlying mechanisms for microbiota-driven behavioral adaptation remain elusive. We previously observed that female Plagiodera versicolora leaf beetles preferentially oviposit on mature leaves despite feeding on new leaves. Here, we demonstrate that this oviposition preference is gut microbiota-dependent, as it is abolished by microbiota depletion and restored by microbiota transplantation.
